note: Only alpha moves. Same mesh, same settings, same area_ref as the production sweep.

usable_range.why: Set by the user on 2026-09-24 and independently supported by the gate: every alpha converged on the RESIDUAL route (6.2-7.8 orders), but the settled-force check fails at alpha 18 (CL 9.5e-2 %) and alpha 20 (CL 1.3e-1 %) against 1.3e-2 % at alpha 14. The forces start to wobble before the residual does, which is what unsteadiness looks like through a steady solver.

stall.reading: CL is still rising at alpha 20 (1.1458) but the increment per 2 degrees is collapsing 0.138 -> 0.083, so CL_max is near 22-24 deg on this geometry. It was not bracketed: alpha 22 was abandoned at ~50 min against a ~21 min norm and alpha 24 was never started, both cancelled on instruction because the range above 15 deg is not wanted.

caveat: Converging is not being correct. Spalart-Allmaras is known to delay stall and over-predict CL_max, and there is no experimental data here to check it against. This scan answers 'can it be run', not 'is it right'.

consequence_for_the_F_FF_matrix.asked: F and FF on both families, 2 geometries, alpha ladder through post-stall = 112 solves, ~318 h at the attached rate and nearer 800 h with separated cases
consequence_for_the_F_FF_matrix.now: With the ladder capped at 15 deg the alphas are -2, 0, 4, 8, 10, 12, 14 = 7, so the matrix is 4 levels x 2 geometries x 7 alphas = 56 solves, ~159 h at 6 ranks. Dropping the FF levels halves it again to 28 solves, ~53 h.
consequence_for_the_F_FF_matrix.recommendation: Deep post-stall is a different study: it needs URANS or DDES and a mesh with a finer wake and wall-normal direction -- the opposite of what family 2 does.
